ky_north_40.blurb: North 40 is a small wall in the southern Red River Gorge, tucked at the end of the Sore Heel trail system within the Pendergrass-Murray preserve. It holds a dozen sandstone routes, mostly bolted with a handful of trad lines. The grade spread is lopsided toward the hard end: five climbs sit around 5.12, with a 5.13 above them, a few 5.10s and 5.11s below, and only two easy routes in the 5.7 to 5.8 range. Expect a quiet, steep amphitheater feel rather than a beginner crag. The walk continues past the neighbouring wall and finishes with a short, steep drop where a hand line helps.

ky_bald_rock_cove.blurb: Bald Rock Cove is a compact sport crag in the Bald Rock preserve of the Red River Gorge, close to the Motherlode and Chocolate Factory. All twelve routes are bolted, and the middle of the range dominates: seven climbs around 5.11, two at 5.10 and three at 5.12. The left side of the cove carries the gentler lines, while the harder ones go through the main cave. The wall faces east, so the vertical section is lit up early and the cave catches the sun by late morning, making it a pleasant choice for a morning session.

ky_front_porch_wall.blurb: Front Porch Wall is one of the thirty-odd walls in Muir Valley, in the Red River Gorge. Its twelve climbs are all bolted, and the spread is unusually wide: three easy 5.4 routes that can be top-roped make it a good spot for newer climbers, a few more moderates follow in the 5.7 to 5.8 range, and the rest climb through 5.10 and 5.11 into several 5.12s and two 5.13s. That mix suits a group with mixed abilities. The approach follows the south trail uphill from the creek crossing, reaching the easy routes first.
